title: IBRANCE Dosing Decisions: Act or Continue?
instruction: For each finding, decide whether the current IBRANCE (palbociclib) prescribing information calls for holding or reducing the dose, or for continuing the current regimen unchanged.

items.prompt: Grade 3 neutropenia recurs on Day 1 of a new 28-day cycle
items.rationale: Label-directed dose modification requires withholding IBRANCE until the neutrophil count recovers to Grade ≤2, then resuming at the next lower dose, when Grade 3 (or recurrent Grade 3) neutropenia occurs on Day 1 of a cycle.

items.prompt: Grade 1 neutropenia only, present through the first six treatment cycles
items.rationale: Per the FDA label, patients with no more than Grade 1 or 2 neutropenia through the first 6 cycles require no dose adjustment; CBC monitoring can shift to every 3 months instead.

items.prompt: New dry cough and exertional dyspnea without fever, suspected pneumonitis
items.rationale: Any new or worsening respiratory symptom suspected to reflect pneumonitis triggers immediate interruption and evaluation, regardless of fever or how mild the symptoms appear.

items.prompt: Child-Pugh class C hepatic impairment identified before the first dose
items.rationale: Child-Pugh C hepatic impairment increases palbociclib exposure enough that the label mandates starting at the reduced 75 mg dose rather than the standard 125 mg.

items.prompt: Child-Pugh class B (moderate) hepatic impairment identified before the first dose
items.rationale: The label specifies no dose adjustment for mild (Child-Pugh A) or moderate (Child-Pugh B) hepatic impairment; only Child-Pugh C impairment requires a dose reduction.

citations.title: Label: IBRANCE- palbociclib tablet, film coated - DailyMed

items.prompt: Creatinine clearance of 25 mL/min identified before starting therapy
items.rationale: The label states no dose adjustment is required for any degree of renal impairment with creatinine clearance greater than 15 mL/min, so this patient's regimen stays the same.

items.prompt: Severe interstitial lung disease confirmed on pulmonary work-up
items.rationale: The label directs permanent discontinuation of IBRANCE, not a temporary interruption, once severe ILD/pneumonitis is confirmed.

items.prompt: Patient requires concurrent itraconazole that cannot be switched or stopped
items.rationale: If a strong CYP3A inhibitor such as itraconazole cannot be avoided, the label instructs reducing the IBRANCE dose because coadministration meaningfully increases palbociclib exposure.
